speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. To help diagnose the cause of your chronic diarrhea and abdominal discomfort, could you describe the consistency and frequency of your stools, and note if you see any blood or mucus? Also, have you experienced any unintentional weight loss or fever recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping history and recent illness in your party, have you noticed any specific food triggers or experienced nausea and vomiting? I would like to check for parasitic infections, so REQUEST TEST: Stool_Ova_and_Parasites.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since the stool tests are normal, I need to rule out inflammatory causes like IBD. Do you experience night-time bowel movements that wake you from sleep, and have you had any joint pain or eye inflammation? REQUEST TEST: Fecal_Calprotectin

speaker: Doctor
text: Since inflammatory markers and parasitic tests are normal, this presentation strongly suggests Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). Do you find that your symptoms are closely linked to stress or anxiety, and have you noticed any specific foods that consistently worsen your symptoms?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the camping exposure and the fact that others in your party fell ill, we must consider Giardia despite the initial normal stool test, as it can be intermittent. REQUEST TEST: Stool_Giardia_Antigen

speaker: Doctor
text: With parasitic and inflammatory causes effectively ruled out, your symptoms align with Irritable Bowel Syndrome, specifically the diarrhea-predominant subtype.
